title: Grateful Dead Live at Manhattan Center on 1971-04-05

ai_review.summary: Crystal‑clear classic ’71 soundboard captures an upbeat, high‑energy show with stellar Garcia tone and three Skull & Roses classics.
ai_review.review: The recording is a pristine soundboard capture that showcases the band at the height of their early‑70s form – tight, lively, and brimming with good‑time music. Reviewers rave about the clean mix, Jerry’s superb guitar tone, and standout performances of “Big Railroad Blues,” “Not Fade Away” and the third Skull & Roses cut. The set flows effortlessly, delivering a fun, well‑rehearsed concert experience.

ai_rating.rationale: All five reviews are overwhelmingly positive (average 4.8 stars), praising both the musical performance and the high‑quality soundboard recording, yielding a strong combined rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Reviewers describe the mix as crisp, clean and upbeat; no dropouts or major issues are noted. Some suggest using EQ for optimal playback, but overall the sound is praised as superb.

show_quality.setlist_flow: An energetic, well‑rehearsed set that moves smoothly through the classic ’71 repertoire, delivering a fun and cohesive concert experience.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia's guitar tone is highlighted as never better than April 1971 – crystal clear and full of energy.
